- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 10–30% for near-term horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0), model often overcorrects with a steep drop; cap forecast decline to 50% of spike magnitude for next 3–5d.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops in 10–30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 5–15% buffer to forecast for long-term (15–30d) if sentiment < 0.5.
- If history shows mean reversion (price oscillating around 1.8–2.0), model tends to overpredict extremes; apply 10–20% dampening to forecast if price deviates > 0.3 from recent 7d average.
- For 30d forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive over last 5d, model often overestimates; apply 20–40% downward adjustment if forecast > 2.5 and true outcome < 1.5.
